S63.02.note: A second route exists: the chat title's More actions menu has 'Schedule…', which opens Shortcuts with the form pre-filled from the chat's first prompt.
steps: Open the side panel and click More, then Shortcuts (this opens the Options page on the Shortcuts section).
Under Schedules, click New schedule.
Type a Name and write the instructions in Instructions.
Pick a Repeat option, fill in the Time, and click Create schedule.
Compare: a message 'Created <name>. It runs in the cloud even when this browser is closed.' appears and the new routine is listed in Schedules.
S63.02.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule

S63.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find the routine in Schedules.
Click Edit on that routine row.
Change the Name, and type or clear the Description (optional) field.
Click Save changes.
Compare: the message 'Saved <name>.' appears and the row shows the new name and description; Edit again shows the saved values.
S63.04.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Edit

S63.05.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Edit on a routine.
Click inside the Instructions box.
Type several lines, pressing Return between them.
Click Save changes, then click Edit again.
Compare: the Instructions box is a multi-line box that keeps all the lines you typed.
S63.05.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Edit > Instructions

labels.text: On chosen days of the week

S63.12.needs: a signed-in AGI account; waiting past a scheduled time to see a run
S63.12.note: The Repeat options in code are Once, Every day, On chosen days of the week and Once a month.
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, then click New schedule.
Fill in Name and Instructions.
Open Repeat and choose Every day (or On chosen days of the week, or Once a month), then fill in Time.
Click Create schedule.
Compare: the routine row shows 'Next <time>' matching the cadence you chose. Whether a run starts at each occurrence is decided on the server and can only be seen later in Runs.
S63.12.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > New schedule > Repeat

S63.19.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Click Run now on its row.
Compare: the message 'Run started.' appears.
Click Runs on the same row and wait for the new run to show a final status.
Compare: the run is listed with status Finished or Failed and its output text.
S63.19.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Run now

S63.20.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
S63.20.note: The Next line is only added to the row when a next time exists.
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and scroll to Schedules.
Read the line 'Next <time>' on each routine row.
Compare the time with the schedule you set in Repeat and Time.
Create a routine with a future time and check that its row shows the new Next time.
S63.20.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row)

S63.21.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a routine that has run (a failed run shows the error line)
S63.21.note: The status badge on the row shows the raw status word from the data (for example 'failed'), not a translated label.
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Read the line 'Last <time>' or 'Not run yet' on its row.
If a run failed, read the 'Last run: <error>' line under it.
Compare with the Runs list: the newest run's time and status should match the row.
S63.21.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row)

S63.23.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a routine that has run at least once
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Runs on a routine row that has run.
Read the run list under the heading Runs.
For each run, read its status (Finished, Failed and so on) and the output text under it.
Compare: each run shows its output text, not only its status.
S63.23.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Runs

S63.24.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine in Schedules.
Click Pause on its row.
Compare: the message 'Schedule paused.' appears and the button changes to Resume; the routine stays in the list.
Click Resume.
Compare: the message 'Schedule resumed.' appears and the button changes back to Pause.
S63.24.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Pause

labels.text: Delete $NAME$ and its run history? This cannot be undone.

S63.27.needs: a signed-in AGI account and one saved routine you can afford to delete
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and click Delete on a routine row.
Read the confirmation 'Delete <name> and its run history? This cannot be undone.'
Click Cancel first and check the routine is still listed.
Click Delete again, then Delete in the confirmation.
Compare: the message 'Deleted <name>.' appears and the routine is gone from the list.
S63.27.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row) Delete

labels.text: Paused until you approve or deny this step

S63.32.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a routine whose unattended run reaches a tool call that needs approval
S63.32.note: The code does not name a simple user action that triggers an approval; the approval comes from the tool-call gate during an unattended run, so the tester may need a routine whose run calls a tool that requires approval.
steps: Open More, then Shortcuts, and find a routine whose run is waiting for approval.
Read the block 'Paused until you approve or deny this step' with its expiry line and the action it asks for.
Click Approve (or Deny).
Compare: the message 'Approved. The run continued.' (or 'Denied. The run continued without that step.') appears, the waiting block goes away, and the run reaches a final status under Runs.
S63.32.where: Side panel: More > Shortcuts > Schedules > (routine row with a waiting run)
